Why You Need a Clay Bar Kit

Washing your car removes surface dirt, but it can't touch the invisible bonded contaminants — rail dust, industrial fallout, brake dust particles, and tree sap residue — that embed themselves into your clear coat. That's where a clay bar comes in. By gently pulling these contaminants out of the paint, a clay bar restores that buttery-smooth, glass-like surface that makes your car look and feel brand new.

Both Chemical Guys and Adam's Polishes sell all-in-one clay bar kits that include the clay, lubricant, and microfiber towel you need to decontaminate your paint in one session. But the formulations, lubricant quality, and overall value differ considerably. Here's how the two stack up.

🛠️ Detailed Breakdown

Clay Quality & Safety

Adam's Polishes uses a proprietary visco-elastic polymer clay that is noticeably softer and more pliable than traditional detailing clay. This means it conforms to panel contours more easily and carries a lower risk of marring — making it the safer choice for first-time clay bar users or those with softer paint finishes (think Japanese and some European cars). That said, the Chemical Guys medium-grade clay is no slouch, and when used with adequate lubrication, it produces equally smooth results on the vast majority of factory paint jobs.

Lubricant Showdown

Here's where the two kits diverge significantly. Chemical Guys includes their dedicated "Clay Luber," a synthetic lubricant engineered specifically for clay bar work. It's slick, it works, and it does exactly what it says. Adam's Polishes includes their iconic Detail Spray — a multi-use product that works brilliantly as clay lubricant and doubles as a quick detailer between washes, a drying aid, or a gloss enhancer. If you value versatility, Adam's gives you more bang for your lubricant buck. If you want a purpose-built, no-fuss clay lubricant, Chemical Guys wins.

Value & Kit Contents

At $29.99, the Chemical Guys Complete System costs $5 less than the Adam's kit and includes more clay (three bars versus two), giving you enough material for 2–3 full vehicles. The included dual-pile microfiber towel is also a cut above — one side for initial wipe-down, the other for final buffing. Adam's counters with USA-made clay and a spray that serves double duty, but for sheer dollar-per-vehicle value, Chemical Guys takes the crown.

Ease of Use

Both kits come with clear instructions and everything you need in one box. The Adam's softer clay is slightly more forgiving for beginners who might apply uneven pressure or let lubrication run thin. Chemical Guys' firmer clay gives you more tactile feedback — you can literally feel when the paint is clean because the clay stops dragging and starts gliding. Both approaches work; it comes down to personal preference. For most weekend warriors, the Chemical Guys instructions and included clay bars provide an excellent learning experience.

🏆 Final Verdict: Chemical Guys Wins on Value

Both kits will leave your paint impossibly smooth and ready for wax or sealant. But the Chemical Guys Clay Bar Kit Complete System edges out Adam's Polishes on overall value. You get more clay, a better microfiber towel, a dedicated clay lubricant that works flawlessly, and you save $5 in the process — enough for a bottle of quick detailer to maintain that glass-smooth finish.

Choose the Adam's Polishes kit if you have a soft or delicate paint finish, you're new to clay bar work and want the lowest marring risk possible, or you love the versatility of a lubricant that doubles as a detail spray. For everyone else — especially experienced DIY detailers doing multiple vehicles — Chemical Guys delivers more for less.

❓ Frequently Asked Questions

How often should I clay bar my car?

Most detailers recommend claying once or twice per year — typically in spring after winter road salt and in fall before applying a protective winter sealant. Perform the baggie test first: put your hand in a plastic sandwich bag and run it over clean paint. If it feels rough or gritty, it's time to clay.

Do I need to polish after claying?

Not necessarily. A gentle clay bar session with plenty of lubrication typically won't marr the paint, especially on factory-hard finishes. But if you're chasing absolute perfection — or if your paint is soft — a light polish before waxing or sealing is recommended to remove any faint clay-induced micro-marring.

Can I reuse clay that's been dropped on the ground?

Never. If a clay bar hits the ground, it picks up abrasive particles that will scratch your paint on the next pass. Both Chemical Guys and Adam's include enough clay that you can afford to toss a contaminated piece and grab a fresh section. Always knead and fold the clay bar frequently to expose a clean working surface.
